slides.chapter: 1. Recognize when lender help would be useful
slides.title: Connect the lender conversation to a specific need
slides.lead: A useful recommendation begins with what the buyer wants to understand.
slides.body:
Understand the reason

“What would you need to know before deciding whether buying fits your plans?” Listen for the question instead of assuming they want to buy now.

Explain the purpose

“A loan officer can help you understand the payment and what would need to happen next. Would that information help you plan?”

Respect their relationship

Ask about a lender they already work with. Offer an introduction when useful and accepted. A buyer can choose to keep their current lender.

slides.chapter: 1. Recognize when lender help would be useful
slides.title: What Zillow Home Loans offers your buyer
slides.lead: Connect Zillow Home Loans to the buyer’s next decision.
slides.body:
A clearer search

BuyAbility can help buyers estimate a budget using current rates. It is a starting point for discussion.

A person on the file

A named loan officer gives the buyer someone to ask about financing and the agent someone to coordinate with.

A coordinated next step

ZHL offers agent collaboration tools and status updates, including connections through Follow Up Boss.

Say the benefit
“Let’s get clear on a comfortable payment and what still needs to happen before you offer.”
ZHL agent tools and BuyAbility ↗
slides.notes:
Keep the ecosystem explanation to one minute. Ask: which of these benefits matters to Jordan right now? Accept a buyer-specific answer. Remove the implication that software removes all friction or that a particular letter automatically wins an offer. A named loan officer and a clear next action are the practical value.

slides.lead: A buyer says, “My bank gave me a letter, so I’m ready to offer tonight.”

1. What do you know from that statement?
  2. What would you ask the loan officer to confirm?
After your answer: review the explanation
Ask what the lender has reviewed, what is still conditional, whether the property affects the review, and what timing the file can support. Let the loan officer confirm the process for this buyer. Avoid promising approval, credit impact or a closing date.

slides.chapter: 2. Know what to explain and what the lender must confirm
slides.title: Pre-qualification, pre-approval, and final approval
slides.lead: These are different stages. Ask what has actually been checked.
slides.body:
Pre-qualification

Zillow describes this as an estimate using self-reported information and a soft credit check. Ask what the buyer has actually completed.

Pre-approval

The lender reviews supporting information and identifies conditions. Ask the loan officer what has been verified and what remains before relying on the letter.

Final approval

The lender must resolve the remaining borrower and property requirements. A pre-approval letter does not guarantee funding. Confirm readiness and timing with the loan officer.

Zillow Home Loans FAQ, reviewed September 16, 2026. Ask the lender to explain credit inquiries for this buyer before they proceed.
slides.notes:
Ask agents to explain the stages without reading them. Correct the idea that a branded letter is a guarantee. Do not claim that all other lenders use unverified information. Fully underwritten pre-approval is another level of review to discuss with the loan officer. Ask: what would you want to know before relying on any letter?
Handoff: Next: Questions for the loan officer. Connect it to the action you just practiced.
slides.cue: Next: Questions for the loan officer. Connect it to the action you just practiced.

slides.chapter: 2. Know what to explain and what the lender must confirm
slides.title: Questions for the loan officer
slides.lead: Know which questions need a loan officer’s answer.
slides.body:
Before the buyer proceeds

“What will you review at this step? Will it involve a soft or hard inquiry, and what should the buyer expect afterward?”

Before relying on a letter

“What has been verified? What documents or conditions remain? Does this property change the review or payment?”

Before committing to timing

“What can you support on this file, and what do you need first?” Give the buyer the confirmed answer rather than a general estimate.
slides.notes:
The source deck’s 585 floor conflicts with the current FAQ, which states 620 for most loan types. Do not replace one blanket cutoff with another in agent scripts. Route eligibility to the lender. The FAQ contains inconsistent wording about hard checks, but explicitly allows circumstances requiring a hard inquiry. Do not use “soft pull always.” Keep product exclusions, exact terms, fee claims and special pricing in the reference review, not memory drills.

slides.title: What would you ask when the buyer already has a lender?
slides.lead: The buyer says, “My bank has handled everything for years. Why would I need another conversation?”

slides.chapter: 3. Offer an introduction and understand concerns
slides.title: Responding to common concerns
slides.lead: Listen first. Answer the concern. Keep the choice with the buyer.
slides.body:
“I already have a lender.”

Acknowledge the relationship. Learn whether anything is still unclear.

“I don’t want a credit hit.”

Understand the concern. Let the loan officer explain the actual process before the buyer decides.

“Are you making me use them?”

The buyer chooses. An introduction is available if it helps.
slides.notes:
Have an agent answer before revealing each coaching example. Ask the buyer role: did that address your actual concern? If not, ask a question instead of pushing harder. Cover all three briefly. On comparison shopping, do not promise to beat a rate or say a comparison is automatically free of credit impact. Have each agent submit one response. Reveal one relevant example, then ask them to retry a specific phrase. Do not measure success by whether the buyer accepts an introduction.

activity.prompt: Choose one buyer concern. Respond in a way that helps them decide.

fields.label: Which concern are you responding to, and what would you say?

activity.model: Already has a lender: “What do you like about working with them, and is there anything you still want clarity on?” If useful, offer an optional second perspective without promising savings. Credit concern: “Is your concern about the first step, or about what happens later in the application?” Let the loan officer explain the process; do not promise every step is free of credit impact. Required lender: “You choose your lender. My role is to help you understand your options. An introduction is available if you want it.” If they decline, respect it and discuss the next step with their chosen lender.

slides.chapter: 4. Complete the handoff and follow through
slides.title: Make the introduction and confirm the call
slides.lead: Permission → introduction → confirmation → follow-through.
slides.body:
Fictional group-message example

Jordan, meet Casey, a loan officer with Zillow Home Loans.

With your permission, I’m connecting you to discuss financing options before your next offer.

Casey, Jordan is available at 3 p.m. Can you confirm whether that works and explain the next steps?

Use your approved referral workflow and the buyer’s agreed contact channel.

Before sending

Get permission and agree how to connect.

After sending

Confirm the loan officer received it and the buyer knows what to expect.

In your CRM

Record consent, owner, agreed next step, and follow-up time.
slides.notes:
Ask: if we send this and hear nothing, who owns the next move? The agent owns checking that the introduction landed, not promising a loan outcome. Do not put financial documents or sensitive account information into a group message. Use the approved lender channel for the application.

slides.chapter: 4. Complete the handoff and follow through
slides.title: Follow up on incomplete introductions
slides.lead: Review where buyers are waiting and who needs to follow up.
slides.body:
Review the dashboard

Review the team’s current dashboard, definitions, and reporting window.

Check incomplete introductions

Look for introductions that stalled, unanswered questions, or an unclear owner.

Confirm the follow-up

Confirm the next step with the buyer and loan officer; update the record accurately.

Illustrative rate exercise

6 issued pre-approvals
÷ 60 eligible buyers

6 ÷ 60 × 100 = 10%. Use the rate to find the records that need follow-up, then inspect what actually happened.

Practice numbers from the source deck, not a verified current program target.
slides.notes:
The original deck specifies 4% conversion, 25% pickup, 10% pre-approval, and a rolling 90-day window. Those exact thresholds, attribution rules, and lead consequences were not established by current public sources. Confirm them in the team’s live dashboard with the program owner. Explain numerator and denominator using the example, without presenting it as a policy. Do not imply agents control approval decisions or should change statuses to improve a metric. Show the illustrative calculation briefly. Spend the discussion on stalled introductions, missing consent or owners, and the next useful action rather than testing arithmetic.

slides.chapter: 4. Complete the handoff and follow through
slides.title: Check financing before writing an offer
slides.lead: Return to Jordan. The buyer wants to write tonight.
slides.body:
Your loan-officer check-in

Readiness

What has been reviewed, and what is still conditional?

This property

Does this property change the payment, eligibility, or review?

Timing

What deadline can you support on this file, and what is needed first?

Say it back to the buyer

Reveal an example

“The loan officer is checking the details for this property and what is still needed. Let’s confirm those items and a workable timeline before we rely on financing terms in the offer.”
slides.notes:
Give 30 seconds to answer before revealing. Invite one person to act as Jordan and another as the agent. Ask Jordan to repeat what happens next; if they cannot, the agent should clarify the handoff. Reinforce that a lender’s average speed is not a promise for this transaction.

slides.title: Practice with a buyer and an observer
slides.lead: Trios: agent, buyer, observer. Switch roles each round.
slides.body:
Observer: score what you hear.

0 / 4 behaviors heard

60-second conversation · 30-second feedback · 30-second retry.
Use “I heard…” and “Try…”
slides.notes:
Allow one minute for roles, three two-minute rounds, and a one-minute debrief. Give every agent a speaking turn, one specific correction, and a targeted retry. Use the meeting platform for breakout rooms. In pairs, the buyer supplies the observation; in trios, rotate agent, buyer, observer. Do not label a peer or self-check as coach sign-off. If no partner is present, assign a coach or leave the observation outstanding. Record what was observed without unsupported claims. A buyer declining an introduction does not fail the attempt; observe how the agent respects that choice.

slides.chapter: 4. Complete the handoff and follow through
slides.title: What do you remember?
slides.lead: Write first. Compare second. Fill the gaps.
slides.body:
Compare with the essentials

Reflect → Explain → Ask → Confirm. A pre-approval is conditional; it does not guarantee funding. A complete handoff includes permission, an identified loan officer, a confirmed next step and owner, and a follow-up time.
slides.notes:
Give 60 seconds with no help. Have partners compare from memory for 30 seconds. Reveal and ask them to fill a gap in a different color on paper, or revise their text. This revisits key ideas after a delay for retrieval, not another lecture. If a gap is common, ask for a fresh example instead of rereading.

slides.lead: Choose a time to practice again without the slides.
slides.body:
Within 24 hours

Deliver your introduction from memory to a partner. Get one correction.

In 3 days

Practice a different objection. Keep buyer choice and a clear next step.

In 7 days

Review one real handoff with your coach. Identify what moved and what stalled.

Download includes your draft, recall answers, and commitment. Live-session submissions are shared with your authorized presenter and coach; a local download stays with you.
slides.notes:
In live sessions, closing the session creates 24-hour recall, three-day fresh-case, and seven-day coach-review assignments. Confirm each agent’s named coach and session timezone. Agents see due work in Rep; the daily digest links to due or reviewable work. In self-paced study, arrange these checks with a coach. Without a relevant client opportunity, use a fresh fictional case and label real-work application not yet observed. Practice readiness is separate from quiz certification and activation.
